issue.title: fix(quill-charts): repaint when the device pixel ratio changes
issue.body:
## Problem

- A chart stays blurry after its window moves to a screen with a different pixel ratio.
- The chart reads the pixel ratio only when it paints, and nothing repaints it when the ratio changes.
- First half of item 50 in #123088.

## Changes

- A chart repaints at the new ratio when the device pixel ratio changes. A browser zoom that leaves the chart's size unchanged is covered too.
- `useChartCanvas` listens to a `resolution` media query and subscribes again after each change, because the query matches one ratio only.
- Every chart type gets this, since they all size their canvas through that hook.

> [!NOTE]
> Not in this PR: the canvas size cap by area, the second half of item 50. It needs a limit chosen per browser and a check on an iOS device.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** one new case in `useChartCanvas.test.tsx` fires the media query change twice and expects a repaint at each new ratio. The closest case covers a restored context, not a ratio change.

- Ran the same listener in headless Chromium with an emulated ratio of 2, 1.5, 1 and 3. It repainted at each one.
- Not checked: a real window moved between two screens.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Fable 5.2 (`claude-fable-5-2`)

**Skills:** `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Decisions:** the listener calls use optional chaining, because some test mocks of `matchMedia` return only `matches`.
- **Read closely:** headless Chromium fires the media query change only when the emulated viewport size changes with the ratio.
- **Follow-ups:** cap the canvas by area in `syncCanvasSize`.
- **No duplicate:** a search of open PRs found none for this fix.
- **CI report:** the bundle grows by 251 B. That is the pixel ratio listener, so nothing can be cut.

</details>

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

issue.title: fix(dashboards): keep a picked sql variable default in the draft
issue.body:
## Problem

On a dashboard that saved a value for a SQL variable, picking the variable's default in the dropdown does nothing: tiles keep the saved value, the chip resets and an unsaved filter banner shows. "Save filters" after that pick wipes the saved value.

Closes #132024

## Changes

- Picking a variable value now always stores it in the dashboard draft, so tiles refresh with the default too and saving keeps the pick.
- Before, a pick equal to the default was dropped from the draft, and the backend read the missing key as "use the saved value".
- The saved/unsaved state and the URL already compare against the saved value or default, so picking the default on a dashboard with nothing saved still reads as saved.

issue.title: fix(insights): stop concurrent patches reverting other fields
issue.body:
## Problem

- Two API or MCP clients that edit different fields of the same insight at the same time can lose one edit. Both PATCHes return 200, but the later save writes back the stale value of the other field.
- A probe against US Cloud raced 11 PATCH pairs on one insight (`name` in one, `description` in the other). In 6 pairs, one write was lost.

## Changes

- An insight PATCH now changes only the fields it sent, also when another request lands first.
- `InsightSerializer.update` locks the row and reloads the instance before it applies the request, the same approach the feature flag serializer uses.
- Cohorts and dashboards have the same pattern and are left for a follow-up.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** `test_patch_does_not_restore_a_field_changed_since_the_read` lands a write between `get_object` and the save, as the feature flag test does. It fails without the fix with `'old description'`. No existing test covered the stale read.

- Ran the insight API tests that match update, patch, tags, restore, dashboards and activity, locally against Postgres.
- Not run: tests that query ClickHouse, because the local setup had none.

👉 _Stay up-to-date with [PostHog coding conventions](https://posthog.com/docs/contribute/coding-conventions) for a smoother review._

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5

**Skills:** `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Session:** Claude Code with a sparse checkout and a local Postgres.
- **Decisions:** A version precondition, like notebooks use, would also cover the web app's full-object saves. That is a larger design choice, so this PR fixes partial PATCHes only.
- **Decisions:** A search of open PRs and issues found no fix for this race.
- **Follow-ups:** the same fix for `CohortSerializer.update` and `DashboardSerializer.update`.

issue.title: quill-charts improvements: simplify, clean up api, performance bugs etc
issue.body:
Tracks the open work on `@posthog/quill-charts`. Two reviews feed it, and their detailed reports are in the comments below, with file and line evidence.

- **Review 1** (master `9349718f19fd`): the public API and its ~315 consumer files, the internals, and the React layer, tests and docs. Reports `API`, `INT` and `RTD`.
- **Review 2** (master `661cf9b6a0ae`): accessibility and locale, behaviour at scale and with bad data, how chart types share code, and what consumers write around the library. Report `R2`. Its items start at 46.

Codes like `INT H1` point into those reports. Item numbers are stable ids, not an order: the sections are in the order to do them, and finished items move to "Done" at the bottom. Sizes: S under a day, M a few days, L a week or more. Each item is one PR unless noted.

## Ground rules

- **Avoid breaking changes.** The desktop app and web canvases pin the package from npm. A rename adds the new name, keeps the old one working as `@deprecated`, and removes it after both bump. A real break is decided case by case.
- **The custom chart kit stays public.** Generated canvas charts build on `Chart`, `RadialChart`, `drawGrid`, `drawAxes`, `applyChartDefaults`, the core types and the tooltip pieces (#120197, #121121). "0 consumers in the repo" undercounts anything a canvas skill teaches, so check the canvas skills before removing an export. See open question 1.
- **Wrapper charts keep their error boundary** and also pass `onError` to the chart they wrap.
- **No React Compiler for now.** Memo cleanup is manual, guarded by a repaint-count test (item 8).
- **Real components in their own files**, not `renderX()` helpers. Memo only where identity matters: effect dependencies, context values, canvas redraw inputs and memoized child props.

## What shapes the work

- `Chart` re-renders on every mousemove, because hover state lives in its body. That is why some of its memos are needed. Item 29 fixes this at the root.
- Sharing is good at the bottom (canvas hook, shell, legend, theme, line and bar drawing) and thin in the middle. Each cartesian chart assembles its own grid, axes, hover and click routing, and four charts build their own base (`R2 A`).
- Labels are both the x position key and the display text, and time is only tick text. That causes the most consumer workarounds (`R2 X`).
- Three shared files are still large: `canvas-renderer.ts` (1,610 lines), `scales.ts` (921) and `types.ts` (719). The placement rules are fixed (item 22). The split is item 23.

## 1. Bugs

- [ ] 47. Bad values draw a wrong picture. Stacked and percent layouts clamp negatives to 0 while value labels print the real number, a `NaN` in a stacked line dives to the baseline, and non-positive values on a log axis draw at the axis floor. Show them as they are, or as gaps. (S, `R2 B2`)
- [ ] 50. A chart stays blurry after its window moves to a screen with a different pixel ratio, and the canvas size cap is by side, not by area. Listen for the resolution change and cap by area. (S, `R2 B5`) Not reproduced: #132433 was closed. A browser zoom already repaints through the resize path, so check the screen move on real hardware before fixing.

## 2. Safety net

- [ ] 51. A dev-only input check in `Chart`: warn once for duplicate series keys, duplicate labels and `data.length !== labels.length`. These are the top AGENTS.md gotchas, and today they fail silently. (S, `R2 S1`)
- [ ] 52. A benchmark in the package at 100k points × 10 series and 100 points × 1k series, over scales, stacks, label thinning and the static draw. Land it before section 10. (S, `R2 S2`)
- [ ] 53. Guard the public surface: an export snapshot test, a changelog, and a README in the published package. Today a removed export fails nothing until the desktop app bumps. (S, `R2 S3`)

## 3. Delete what nobody uses

- [ ] 9. Dead internals: `ChartProps.labelToCoord` (no caller, 23 references), the bar baseline-rounding path, `findNearestIndex`, `withVerticalClip`'s `pad`. `drawGrid` takes `valueTicks` instead of a duck-typed d3 fallback. About 130 lines. (S, `INT D1`)
- [ ] 10. Unused exports and options that no canvas skill teaches, for example the pie and sankey layout helpers, `useChart`, three per-chart tooltips, `fillStyle` gradient/gloss, the unused BoxPlot and Pie knobs. Deprecate, then remove. (S, `API A1`, `A3`, `C4`)

## 4. Consumer quick wins (additive)

- [ ] 54. Charts fill a block parent that has a height, not only a flex column: `h-full` on the root, or `height?: number | 'fill'` on every chart. About 65 consumer files add a `flex flex-col` wrapper for this today. (S, `R2 C1`, `API E1`)
- [ ] 11. Optional `theme` read from a provider. Then a codemod removes `theme={theme}` from 216 call sites in 133 files, about 300 lines. (S plus M, `API B1`) Library part merged in #125455. Next: item 55, then mount `ChartThemeProvider` at the app root (nothing mounts it yet), then the codemod (207 `theme={theme}` sites on master).
- [ ] 55. The provider also carries `onError` and `timezone`. About three quarters of call sites report no errors, and 50 of 61 time-series files thread `timezone` by hand. Do it before item 11's codemod, so call sites are swept once. (S, `R2 C3`)
- [ ] 13. Reduce `margins` to primitives inside the charts, so consumers need not memoize config. Then sweep about 100 config lines that restate defaults. (S, `API B3`) Library part merged in #125454. The defaults sweep follows.
- [ ] 44. Resolve series colours once, where the base colours the series: palette, then `var()`, then sRGB, against the chart wrapper and again on theme change, for every chart. About 50 consumer files resolve CSS variables or index the palette by hand today. This replaces the chart-by-chart port described in the gauge follow-ups comment. (M, `R2 A4`, `C2`) The fallback half merged in #129017.
- [ ] 56. Tooltip rows and value labels default to the format of the series' own y-axis, and `YAxisFormat` gains `bytes`. 17 consumer files pass the same formatter two or three times. (S, `R2 C4`, `API B5`)
- [ ] 57. Type `Series.data` as `(number | null)[]` and document that null is a gap. The charts already tolerate null (#126983), but consumers map it to `NaN` or to 0 because the type says `number[]`. (S, `R2 C5`)
- [ ] 58. A shared base props type for every chart, so `className`, `dataAttr`, `onError` and new shared props such as `height` (item 54) and `ariaLabel` (item 65) are added once. (S, `API B9`)
- [ ] 59. A marker overlay whose x can fall between labels and whose label is a node, plus `plotRight` and `plotBottom` on `dimensions`. At least 7 consumer files rebuild this. (M, `R2 C6`)
- [ ] 60. `Series.opacity` and a `highlightedKeys` option, so consumers stop turning hex into rgba to dim a series. (S, `R2 C7`)

## 5. Simplify the internals

- [ ] 16. `useChartInteraction`: a 14-argument tooltip builder called twice, a 130-line click handler, 9 noise memos. About 80 lines. (S, `INT I1`)
- [ ] 19. Replace `ChartScales._private` with a generic `Chart<S extends ChartScales>`: `createScales` returns `S`, and the draw functions and tooltip get `S`. Each chart adds its own fields (`d3`, `layout`) next to `x`/`y`, so 16 casts, 9 nested wrapper types and the `if (!priv) return` guards go. Non-scale state (Sankey's `linkOpacity`, `hasEmphasis`) moves out of the scales. `S` defaults to `ChartScales` and `_private` stays `@deprecated` until canvas bumps, so custom charts keep compiling. Until then, add no new uses of `_private`. The gauge (#123010) added one. (S to M, `INT C2`)
- [ ] 20. Handle orientation with a transpose instead of mirrored branches in `drawGrid`, `cornersFor` and `roundOuterStackCaps`. About 110 lines. (S, `INT C3`)
- [ ] 21. Fold `buildBarValueScale` into `buildValueScale` and share the range accumulator. About 45 lines. (S, `INT S2`)
- [ ] 61. The base draws the grid before and the axes after a chart's series pass. Five charts assemble the same two blocks by hand, and the copies have drifted. Keep `drawStatic` working for custom charts. Fits item 9's `valueTicks` change. (M, `R2 A1`)
- [ ] 62. One bar layer in core (stack data, static draw, hover, tooltip narrowing, click routing), used by BarChart and ComboChart. Bars in a combo then gain segment hover, the context menu, drag-zoom and tracks. (M, `R2 A2`)
- [ ] 63. Small shared pieces: one chrome-off config for the three presets, one hover-animation resolver that returns 0 under reduced motion, one hover-emphasis helper for Pie and Sankey, and one base tooltip config type. (S, `R2 A5`, `API B7`, `B8`)

## 6. Restructure files

- [ ] 23. Split `canvas-renderer.ts`, `scales.ts` and `types.ts` by concern, and move single-chart code next to its chart. 3 PRs. (M, `INT C1`)
- [ ] 24. Turn render helpers into components: the inline tooltip adaptors in BarChart, Heatmap, ProportionBar, ScatterChart and BoxPlot (pure narrowing function plus named component), and the multi-component files `ReferenceLine.tsx` (7 components), `FunnelChart.tsx`, `PieChart.tsx`, `MetricCard/internals.tsx`, Legend and tooltip rows. One PR per file. Export the shared tooltip row and a header, which consumers also rebuild. (M, `RTD C1`, `C2`, `R2 C9`)
- [ ] 25. Pull pure layout out of `ValueLabels.tsx` (400 of 611 lines) and `AxisLabels.tsx`. One positioned-label component replaces 7 copies of label styles. One number formatter replaces 11 copies. (M, `RTD D3`, `E1`, `E3`)

## 7. Tests, docs, stories

- [ ] 27. Remove legend tests duplicated in 7 chart files, CSS-class tests, and two tests that inspect the canvas against `TESTING.md`. (S, `RTD F3`, `F4`)
- [ ] 28. Fix stale docs (for example a Sparkline `width` prop that does not exist), widen the AGENTS.md memoize rule to every input the scales read, and cut about 500 lines of story boilerplate. (S plus M, `RTD G`, `H2` to `H5`)

## 8. Bigger design changes, in order

- [ ] 29. Move hover state out of the `Chart` body, so a mousemove re-renders only the interaction layer. About 8 more memos stop being needed. (M, `INT P1`)
- [ ] 30. One `hitTest` seam for "what is under the cursor". It replaces `resolveHoverIndex`, `wrapClickData`, `resolveBottomValue` and `bandSlotAtCursor`, and BarChart stops resolving the hovered bar in 4 places per mousemove. The biggest win for custom charts. 3 PRs. (L, `INT X1`)
- [ ] 31. One multi-axis resolver in place of 5 copies that comments call "mirrors". 2 PRs. (M, `INT S1`)
- [ ] 32. Canvas-layer hooks that take paint closures, so Pie, Sankey, Gauge and FlameGraph stop faking `ChartScales` and the layout context. Keep `RadialChart` public. Then one shared pointer hook for the four interaction paths, on pointer events so drag-zoom works on touch. A small first step: `ChartShell` provides the theme, which removes four copied stub contexts. (S, then M, then L, `INT R1`, `I3`, `R2 A3`, `Y4`)
- [ ] 64. Position by index, not by label string. Labels are the x position key and the display text, so about 15 consumer files invent keys, and one SQL chart asks the end user to cast values in SQL. Steps: `xAt(index)` on the scales so labels can repeat, an optional `xTicks()` so Scatter stops faking labels, then `xForTime(ms)` and reference lines between labels. Do it with item 30, because both change the scales contract. 3 PRs. (L, `R2 X`)
- [ ] 33. One nested `xAxis`/`yAxis` config across every cartesian chart, with the flat keys deprecated, and one name per option (`scale`, `domain`, `startAtZero`). Then fold the `TimeSeries*` wrappers into the base charts, keeping the old names as aliases. The end state, after item 62, is one cartesian chart with a type per series: 11 consumer files branch between two components today to offer a line or bar toggle. (M each, `API C1`, `C2`, `C3`, `R2 C8`)
- [ ] 34. One drag-select callback in the core. Consumers get `onRangeSelect` (x only) and `onAreaSelect` (2D) instead of five names; old names deprecated. (M, `API D3`)
- [ ] 35. Move the files that use quill-charts `MetricCard` to the composable quill-components `Metric`, and mark `MetricCard` and the six helpers exported only for it `@deprecated`. Remove them after the desktop app and canvas bump. Decided in #127416: `Metric` wins. (M, `API A5`) The in-app tiles moved and `MetricCard` is deprecated in #127450. Left: three desktop app files, then the removal.

## 9. Accessibility and locale

- [ ] 65. An `ariaLabel` prop with a truthful default per chart (Heatmap and BarList read wrongly today), `aria-pressed` on legend rows, and table semantics on the legend table. First move the test accessor's series count from the label text to a data attribute. (S, `R2 Y1`)
- [ ] 66. Keyboard access: the chart is one tab stop, arrow keys move the hover index, Enter runs the click, Escape clears, and pinned tooltip rows become buttons. No chart can be operated by keyboard today. After item 30. (L, `R2 Y2`)
- [ ] 67. Tell series apart by more than colour: an opt-in cycle of dash and marker by series index, and legend and tooltip swatches that draw the series' own stroke and marker. (M, `R2 Y3`)
- [ ] 68. One locale. Axis ticks use `en-US` and tooltips the browser locale, so one chart can show `1,500.5` beside `1.500,5`. Read one `locale` in item 25's formatter, then add a `localeText` map for about 40 fixed English strings. (S then M, `R2 Y5`)

## 10. Scale

The guide's target is 1,000 series × 100,000 points. Hover meets it. The static side thins nothing, so it does full-size work on every pass. Land item 52 first.

- [ ] 69. Static paint: a per-index x pixel array shared by line, area and points, then min and max per pixel column when points exceed about twice the plot width, and one path per style for markers and bars. (M, `R2 P1`)
- [ ] 70. Labels: pick candidates by stride before formatting and measuring (value labels and x-axis labels), cache text widths, and parse dates once per `labels` array. 2 PRs. (M, `R2 P2`)
- [ ] 71. Resize: compute value ranges and stacks once per data change, and only re-range the scales on resize. (M, `R2 P3`)
- [ ] 72. Smaller: Scatter allocates a `NaN` array of total points for every series, and tooltip and legend rows are not windowed past a few hundred series. (S to M each, `R2 P4`)

## Open questions

1. #116505, #120197 and #121121 are closed, and no file outside the library builds on `Chart` or `RadialChart`. Does the "custom chart kit stays public" rule still have a user? If the plan is parked, items 19, 30, 32, 61 and 64 can change `ChartProps` and `ChartScales` without a deprecation step.
2. About 45 consumer files hand-build an empty state beside a chart. The first review kept "no empty prop". Is an `empty` slot, rendered in the chart's own box, worth it? (`R2`, open question 2)

## Done

<details>
<summary>27 items</summary>

- [x] 1. `onError` passes through SlopeChart, Sparkline and MetricCard. (`RTD A1`, `F2a`) #123099
- [x] 2. Scatter hover no longer searches every point per frame. (`RTD A3`) #125205
- [x] 3. Tooltip rows rebuild only when the index changes. (`INT I2`) #125205
- [x] 4. `TimeSeriesComboChart` stops rebuilding scales on every parent render. (`RTD A2`) #125205
- [x] 5. `AxisTitles`, `SankeyColumnLabels` and `SankeyNodeLabels` are memoized. (`RTD A4`) #125205
- [x] 6. The hatch-pattern cache is capped. (`INT C4`) #125205
- [x] 7. Pie has tap-to-reveal on touch and the interactive-overlay click guard. (`INT I3`) #125293
- [x] 8. A no-static-repaint test, as one hover case each in the Pie and Sankey tests rather than an 18-chart test. A render-cost benchmark against master is in a comment on #125334. (`RTD F2b`) #125329
- [x] 12. `config.tooltip` forwards every static `DefaultTooltip` option. (`API B2`) #125452
- [x] 14. BoxPlot and SlopeChart apply the shared defaults. (`API B6`) #125453
- [x] 15. `useHoverAnimation` simplified. (`INT H1`) #129014
- [x] 17. `useChartMargins` is one pure `computeMargins` plus two memos. (`INT H3`) #129015
- [x] 18. Noise memos removed across the React layer. (`RTD B`, `INT M1`) #125334
- [x] 22. CONTRIBUTING.md placement rules rewritten. (`RTD H1`) #123091
- [x] 26. Tests see each chart's real tooltip. (`RTD F1`) #123134
- [x] 36. `./testing` is in `package.json` `exports`. (`API F2`) #125304
- [x] 37. One setup call, `setupChartTests()`. (`API F1`) #123134
- [x] 38. The chart root carries its label count, so hover, click and drag work under any wrapper. #123134
- [x] 39. `await findChart({ seriesCount? })`. #123134
- [x] 40. `await chart.hoverTooltip(i)`. #123134
- [x] 41. Chart-specific readers moved under `chart.sankey`, `chart.slope` and `chart.pie`. #125304
- [x] 42. `TESTING.md` opens with a quick start, and the insight test helpers use the new API. #125304
- [x] 43. The testing API dropped the old "hog chart" name. #123132
- [x] 45. One palette fallback, `DEFAULT_CHART_COLORS[0]`. #129017
- [x] 46. The short-number format no longer hangs on an infinite value, or prints "undefined" past 1e27. (`R2 B1`) #132417
- [x] 48. A chart recovers from a render error when its data changes. Every boundary takes its data prop as `resetKey`, compared with `Object.is`. (`R2 B3`) #132422
- [x] 49. Server rendering no longer throws: text measuring skips the canvas when there is no `document`. The `renderToString` smoke test was left out, because nothing in the repo renders charts on the server. (`R2 B4`) #132427

</details>

## Keep as is

Columnar `Series[]` keyed by `key`; the static and hover canvases; the layout and hover context split; `useChartCanvas`'s resize, pixel-ratio and context-restore handling; `tooltip` as a render prop; domain-named click callbacks and data props; `BarList` over `StackedBarList` over `BarChart`; Sankey on its own path; Gauge, FlameGraph and Histogram as their own charts. The reports give the reasons.

# quill-charts review 2: what the first review did not cover

Lens: accessibility, input and locale; behaviour at scale and with bad data; how well chart types share code; what consumers write around the library; packaging.

Method: four read-only audits plus a pass over the public surface, with each claim below then checked against the source. Library paths are relative to `packages/quill/packages/charts/src/`, with line numbers at master `661cf9b6a0ae`. Consumer counts come from regex scans over about 310 files that import the package, so treat them as close, not exact. Nothing was run in a browser. Two things were run: `renderToString` against the built package (B4) and a tree-shaking measurement ("Checked and fine"). Scale costs are estimates.

## B. Bugs

**B1. The short-number format hangs on an infinite value.**
- `utils/format.ts:152`: `while (Math.abs(value) >= 1000) { magnitude++; value /= 1000 }` never ends for `Infinity`.
- It is reachable through `buildYTickFormatter({ format: 'short' })` (`utils/y-formatters.ts:78`), which also formats tooltip rows, value labels and legend table values.
- `COMPACT_NUMBER_MAGNITUDES` (`utils/format.ts:6`) has 9 entries, so a value of 1e27 or more prints "undefined" as its suffix.

**B2. Bad values draw a wrong picture.**
- Stacked and percent layouts clamp negatives to 0: `core/scales.ts:569`, `row[s.key] = allowNegative ? raw : Math.max(0, raw)`. The segment resolver (`core/scales.ts:631`) then returns 0, so the tooltip shows 0 while `ValueLabels` prints the raw value.
- `NaN` passes that line, d3 emits `NaN` for the layer top, and `core/scales.ts:583` flattens it to 0. A stacked line dives to the baseline instead of breaking. Bars are fine: `core/bar-layout.ts:341` checks the raw value.
- Log scales clamp (`core/scales.ts:369`, `:867`), so zero and negative values draw at the axis floor instead of as gaps.
- After: use the diverging stack when any visible value is negative, or return the raw value from the resolver. Keep non-finite values as gaps through the stack. Map non-positive values on a log axis to a gap.

**B3. A chart that hits a render error stays broken.**
- `core/ChartErrorBoundary.tsx:38` resets only when `resetKey` changes.
- 16 components wrap themselves in the boundary, and 2 pass a key: `charts/SankeyChart/SankeyChart.tsx:61` and `charts/FlameGraph/FlameGraph.tsx:165`.
- On the other 14, one throw from a custom `tooltip` render prop leaves "Something went wrong rendering this chart" until the component remounts. New data does not bring the chart back.
- After: each boundary passes its data prop as `resetKey`, with one parameterized test over all charts.

**B4. Server rendering throws.**
- `utils/text-measure.ts:19` calls `document.createElement('canvas')` with no guard, though the comment below it promises a fallback for SSR.
- It runs during render, through `categoryLabelWidths` (`core/hooks/useChartMargins.ts:234`).
- `renderToString` on the built package: `LineChart`, `BarChart`, `Sparkline` and `BarList` throw `ReferenceError: document is not defined`. `PieChart`, `Gauge`, `SankeyChart`, `FlameGraph` and `Legend` render.
- After: a `typeof document` guard, and a `renderToString` smoke test next to `check:node-import`.

**B5. Pixel ratio.**
- `core/hooks/clearCanvas.ts:16` reads `window.devicePixelRatio` only at paint time, and nothing listens for a resolution change. A chart stays blurry after its window moves between a 1x and a 2x screen, until something else repaints it.
- `core/canvas-size.ts:31` caps the ratio by the longer side only. A browser that limits canvas area, such as Safari on iOS, can still get a blank canvas from a tall chart at a high ratio. Not tested on a device.

## S. Safety net

**S1. No input validation.**
- The package has no dev-only warning anywhere. Its only `console` call is the error boundary's.
- Duplicate series keys overwrite each other in the stack table (`core/scales.ts:569`), so one series' data is lost.
- Duplicate labels collapse on the point scale (`core/scales.ts:146`) and draw the line backwards.
- AGENTS.md lists both under "Gotchas that bite".
- After: a dev-only check in `Chart` that warns once for duplicate keys, duplicate labels and `data.length !== labels.length`.

**S2. No benchmark.**
- The package's only script is `build`, and the largest test fixtures hold a handful of points. The render-cost numbers from item 8 live in a PR comment.
- After: a small suite at 100k points × 10 series and 100 points × 1k series, over `createScales`, the stack builder, `computeVisibleXLabels`, value label candidates, and the static draw against a recording context.

**S3. Nothing guards the public surface.**
- There is no export snapshot test. A removed or renamed export fails nothing here and reaches the desktop app when it bumps.
- There is no changelog.
- `package.json` ships only `dist`, and the README sits in `src/`, so the published package has no README.

## C. What consumers write around the library

**C1. Charts collapse to zero height in a block parent.**
- `core/chart-shell.tsx:7`: the root is `relative w-full flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-hidden`, with no height.
- About 65 of the 114 production files that render a chart wrap it in a `flex flex-col` div with a height. 16 carry a comment saying why, for example `RateLimitHistoryChart.tsx:68` and the desktop app's `MetricChart.tsx:80`.
- `docs/axes.md:69` says an explicit height on the wrapper is enough.
- After: `h-full` beside `flex-1`, or `height?: number | 'fill'` on every chart (`API E1`).

**C2. Colours.** A4 has the library side.
- About 50 production files resolve `var(--…)` or index `theme.colors[n]` by hand before they pass `color`.
- 15 of them memoize the resolved colour without the theme as a dependency, for example `OperationHistogram.tsx:55`. They probably keep the old colour after a light/dark switch. This is read from the dependency lists, not run.
- `VolumeSparkline.tsx:34` hard-codes a hex because the token is `oklch()`.

**C3. App-wide defaults are passed chart by chart.**
- `onError` is set on about 36 of 158 production call sites. The rest get a `console.error` and the fixed English fallback.
- 50 of 61 files that render a `TimeSeries*` chart thread `timezone` by hand.
- Nothing mounts `ChartThemeProvider` yet (item 11).
- After: the provider also carries `onError` and `timezone`. Do it before item 11's codemod, so call sites are swept once.

**C4. The tooltip does not inherit the axis format (`API B5`).**
- `overlays/DefaultTooltip.tsx:75` defaults to `value.toLocaleString()`, whatever the axis shows.
- 17 production files pass the same formatter to the y-axis and to `tooltip.valueFormatter`, for example `PrecomputeTrends.tsx:128-129`. 10 pass it a third time to value labels.
- `humanizeBytes` is passed 7 times, and there is no `bytes` format.
- After: tooltip rows and value labels default to the formatter of the series' own y-axis.

**C5. Missing values.**
- `core/types.ts:49` types `Series.data` as `number[]`. The charts tolerate a null and draw it as a gap on an unstacked line (see #126983), but the type and the docs do not say so.
- About 12 files map null to `NaN` by hand (`sqlLineGraphAdapter.ts:276`). The metrics product draws gaps as 0, because the type has no null (`TimeSeriesPanel.tsx:34`).
- After: `(number | null)[]`, documented.

**C6. Markers.**
- 19 production files read `useChartLayout`, and at least 7 are a labelled marker at a data position.
- `ReferenceLine` resolves x through `scales.x(label)` (`overlays/ReferenceLine.tsx:294`), so it can only sit on a label, and its label is a string. `BillingPeriodMarkers.tsx:61` and `ReportChartMarkers.tsx:18` rebuild it for those two reasons.
- `SpendTrajectoryMarker.tsx:24` recomputes `plotLeft + plotWidth`.
- After: `plotRight` and `plotBottom` on `dimensions`, a marker whose x can fall between labels and whose label is a node, and a wrapper component in place of the `data-hog-charts-interactive-overlay` attribute.

**C7. Dimming.**
- 8 production files turn a hex into rgba to dim a comparison series or to highlight one (`compareDimming.ts:8`). The MCP apps keep their own `fadedColorAt`.
- The library's `comparisonOf` dimming exists only on `TimeSeriesLineChart`.
- After: `Series.opacity`, and a `highlightedKeys` option that fades the rest.

**C8. One chart, two components.**
- 11 production files branch between `TimeSeriesLineChart` and `TimeSeriesBarChart` over the same series, to offer a line or bar toggle. Two cast the config between the two types (`MetricsSeriesChart.tsx:82`).
- `ComboChart` has no direct consumer.
- This is the consumer side of A2 and item 33.

**C9. Custom tooltips.**
- 18 production files build a tooltip from `TooltipSurface`. Only the surface, swatch and footer are exported.
- 2 consumer files define their own `TooltipRow` (`questionVizTooltips.tsx:17`, `FunnelTooltip.tsx:13`), as do `charts/ScatterChart/ScatterTooltip.tsx:15` and `charts/Gauge/GaugeTooltip.tsx:47` inside the library.
- Item 24 already plans the shared row. Export it, with a header.

## A. How chart types share code

Sharing is good at the bottom: one canvas hook, one DOM shell, one legend hook, one theme hook, shared line and bar drawing, and nothing in `core/` imports from `charts/`. It is thin in the middle.

**A1. Grid and axis lines are assembled by hand in five charts.**
- The same `drawGrid` block before the series and `drawAxes` block after them:
  - `charts/LineChart/LineChart.tsx:198` and `:228`
  - `charts/BarChart/utils/draw-bar-chart.ts:141` and `:237`
  - `charts/ComboChart/ComboChart.tsx:233` and `:287`
  - `charts/BoxPlot/BoxPlot.tsx:273` and `:310`
  - `charts/ScatterChart/ScatterChart.tsx:182` and `:211`
- The base already adds tick marks and the crosshair around the chart's draw.
- The copies have drifted. The base picks visible labels with five arguments (`core/Chart.tsx:269`). Bar and Combo use three (`draw-bar-chart.ts:52`, `ComboChart.tsx:230`). With rotated or truncated labels, grid lines can sit on different labels than the tick marks.
- After: `Chart` draws the grid before and the axes after a series pass. Keep `drawStatic` working for charts that call `drawGrid` themselves.

**A2. `ComboChart` is a second, smaller bar chart.**
- `charts/BarChart/BarChart.tsx:427-443` wires `BarTooltip`, `wrapClickData` and `resolveHoverIndex`. `ComboChart` wires none, so a click reports the first visible series (`core/interaction.ts:219`).
- Its hover repeats the bar highlight: `ComboChart.tsx:377` and `draw-bar-chart.ts:294` are the same line. It imports one helper from BarChart's folder (`ComboChart.tsx:60`).
- Bars in a combo have no segment hover, context menu, drag-zoom, tracks, `minBarSize` or legend.
- After: one bar layer in core (stack data, static draw, hover, tooltip narrowing, click routing) that both charts call, the way line drawing already works. That is the step before one cartesian chart with a type per series.

**A3. Four charts build their own base.** This strengthens item 32, which names three.
- The same stub layout context is built in `core/RadialChart.tsx:152`, `charts/SankeyChart/SankeyChart.tsx:278`, `charts/Gauge/Gauge.tsx:401` and `charts/FlameGraph/FlameGraph.tsx:565`. It exists only so `Tooltip` (`overlays/Tooltip.tsx:30`) and `TooltipSurface` (`overlays/TooltipSurface.tsx:26`) can read `theme` from it.
- `FlameGraph.tsx:289` re-implements the static paint loop of `core/hooks/useChartDraw.ts:66`.
- Gauge (`Gauge.tsx:353`) and FlameGraph (`FlameGraph.tsx:421`) keep hover in local state and skip `useTooltipLifecycle`. They have no dismissal on scroll and no tap-to-reveal on touch.
- First step: `ChartShell` provides the theme and the two overlays read it. That removes the four stubs.
- The shared surface also needs an imperative repaint (FlameGraph scroll) and a time-driven one (the gauge tween).

**A4. Colour handling differs per chart.**
- Palette by index is written in `core/chart-shell.tsx:21`, `charts/BarList/BarList.tsx:79`, `components/Legend/legendItemsFromSeries.ts:17` and `charts/ScatterChart/ScatterChart.tsx:223`.
- `var()` is resolved by Heatmap (`Heatmap.tsx:282`), Scatter (`scatter-layout.ts:119`) and Gauge's own wrapper-scoped resolver (`gauge-colors.ts:58`). Line, Bar, Combo, BoxPlot and Pie resolve nothing.
- Two helpers make modern colour syntax parseable: `toSrgbColor` (`core/color-utils.ts:63`) and Sankey's `parseableColor` (`draw-sankey.ts:110`).
- After: resolve once where the base colours the series (palette, then `var()`, then sRGB), against the chart wrapper, and again on theme change. One exported resolver covers non-series colours. This replaces the chart-by-chart port in item 44.

**A5. Small copies.**
- **Chrome switches.** `ProportionBar.tsx:137`, `StackedBarList.tsx:112` and `Sparkline.tsx:52` each list every switch as off. A new default-on switch in `DEFAULT_CHART_CONFIG` shows up in all three until someone notices. After: one exported chrome-off config.
- **Hover fade.**
  - `animateHover` is on the shared config, but only BarChart draws with the fade progress (`BarChart.tsx:339`). Heatmap and Scatter draw with it and never pass a duration.
  - The 150 ms default is declared three times: `core/Chart.tsx:47`, `PieChart.tsx:92`, `SankeyChart.tsx:32`.
  - Reduced motion is honoured by the number tween (`core/hooks/useAnimatedNumber.ts:14`) and not by the hover fade (`core/hooks/useHoverAnimation.ts:63`).
  - After: one resolver that returns 0 under reduced motion. `API B7` covers the option names.
- **Hover emphasis.** Pie and Sankey both dim the rest and brighten the focus, with the same constants (`PieChart.tsx:100`, `draw-sankey.ts:22`).
- **Tooltip config.** `tooltip?: { enabled?: boolean }` is typed inline in `PieChart.tsx:61`, `ProportionBar.tsx:31`, `BarList.tsx:19` and `Gauge.tsx:66` (`API B8`). `PieTooltip` is the default tooltip of two other charts by cross-folder import (`ProportionBar.tsx:19`, `SankeyChart.tsx:15`).

## X. The x-axis

**X1. Labels are both the position key and the display text.**
- `core/scales.ts:146` builds a point scale over the label strings, and `ChartScales.x` takes a label.
- About 15 production files work around it:
  - 5 pass index keys and map them back in formatters (`StoryEvidenceChart.tsx:21`).
  - 5 swap display labels for ISO days (`TrendsLineChart.tsx:159`).
  - The SQL box plot shows the end user an error that asks them to cast values in SQL (`sqlBoxPlotAdapter.ts:172`).
- Chart.js and ECharts position categories by index, so repeated labels are fine there.

**X2. The base has no continuous x-axis.**
- `charts/ScatterChart/ScatterChart.tsx:137` passes one label per point, blanks the base axis (`:296`) and renders its own tick labels (`ScatterXAxisLabels.tsx:34`).
- Line charts have a time scale (`xScale: 'time'`, #127292). It still looks positions up by label, and bars and overlays do not have it.

**X3. Time is only tick text.**
- Three products interpolate time to x by hand: `buildTimePositioner.ts:1`, `BillingPeriodMarkers.tsx:61`, `MetricsExemplarMarkers.tsx:89`.
- One draws its own lines over a `ScatterChart` to get a series over time (`OfflineScoreTrendLines.tsx:16`).

After, in steps:
1. `xAt(index)` on the scales, with `x(label)` kept as a lookup, so labels can repeat.
2. An optional `xTicks()` that axis labels, tick marks and the grid read, so Scatter stops faking labels.
3. `xForTime(ms)` on the layout context, and reference lines that take a position between labels.

Do it with item 30, because both change the scales contract.

## Y. Accessibility, input and locale

**Y1. Screen readers get a count.**
- `core/chart-shell.tsx:97` is `<canvas role="img" aria-label=…>` with no fallback content.
- `core/Chart.tsx:359` hard-codes "Chart with N data series", and no chart takes a label prop.
- Heatmap passes one series per row (`Heatmap.tsx:315`) and BarList one series for all rows (`BarList.tsx:92`), so both read wrongly. Gauge is the good case.
- The tooltip has no role or live region.
- Legend rows are real buttons (`components/Legend/Legend.tsx:142`), but a hidden series shows only as `opacity-40` (`:116`), with no `aria-pressed`. The legend table is nested divs.
- The test accessor parses the label text (`testing/accessor.ts:212`), so move the series count to a data attribute before the default changes.

**Y2. No keyboard path.**
- The shell root (`core/chart-shell.tsx:84-95`) has mouse handlers and no `tabIndex`, role or key handler. The only `tabIndex` in the package is FlameGraph's scroll viewport (`FlameGraph.tsx:603`).
- A keyboard user cannot reach a tooltip, `onPointClick`, `onSliceClick`, a pinned tooltip row (a `div` with a click handler, `overlays/DefaultTooltip.tsx:184`) or drag-zoom.
- Recharts (`accessibilityLayer`) and Highcharts (its accessibility module) make the chart one tab stop and move a hover index with the arrow keys.
- A keyboard index is one more source for item 30's hit test.

**Y3. Series differ by colour only.**
- Colour is `theme.colors[i % length]` (`core/chart-shell.tsx:21`), so series 16 repeats series 1.
- Dash patterns (`core/types.ts:96`) and scatter shapes (`charts/ScatterChart/types.ts:32`) are opt-in. The legend and tooltip swatches (`overlays/TooltipSurface.tsx:59`) draw a plain colour dot either way.
- After: an opt-in cycle of dash and marker by series index, and swatches that draw the series' own stroke and marker.

**Y4. Touch.**
- Drag-to-zoom and the 2D brush use `onMouseDown` plus a window `mouseup` listener (`core/hooks/useDragToZoom.ts:131`), so they have no touch path.
- The legend decides between tap and click from the device, not the event (`components/Legend/useChartLegend.ts:14`). A finger on a touchscreen laptop isolates a series, with no way to add a second one.
- This belongs with item 32's shared pointer hook, on pointer events.

**Y5. Two locales in one chart.**
- Default axis ticks use `en-US` (`core/scales.ts:907`, `utils/format.ts:40`, `:134`). The tooltip and a dozen or so other defaults use the browser locale (`overlays/DefaultTooltip.tsx:75`). A German browser shows `1,500.5` on the axis and `1.500,5` in the tooltip.
- Dates use fixed English patterns (`utils/dates.ts:100`).
- About 40 strings the library renders have no override: legend table headers (`LegendTable.tsx:9`), box plot and gauge tooltip labels (`BoxPlotTooltip.tsx:18`, `GaugeTooltip.tsx:36`), FlameGraph text (`FlameGraph.tsx:622`, `FlameGraphHeader.tsx:111`) and the error fallback.
- After: one `locale` read by item 25's single formatter, then a `localeText` map with English defaults.
- Not checked: `dir="rtl"`, where the DOM parts would flip and the canvas would not.

## P. Scale

The guide's target is 1,000 series × 100,000 points (`docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:30`). Hover meets it. The static side does full-size work on every pass.

**P1. Static paint draws every point.**
- Nothing in `src/` thins the data.
- `tracePath` (`core/canvas-renderer.ts:269`) calls the string-keyed x scale and the y scale for every point. `drawPoints` (`:625`) and `drawArea` (`:485`) walk every point again.
- It starts to matter once points exceed the plot width.
- After: a per-index x pixel array, computed once per scale set and shared by line, area and points. Then min and max per pixel column when points exceed about twice the plot width, and one path per style for markers and bars.

**P2. Labels are formatted and measured for every point.**
- `ValueLabels` builds, formats and measures a candidate per series × index (`overlays/ValueLabels.tsx:225`, `:111`), then checks overlap with a linear scan (`:405`).
- X-axis labels do the same in three places, with no width cache: `computeVisibleXLabels` (`overlays/AxisLabels.tsx:80`), the tick mark pass (`core/Chart.tsx:269`) and margin sizing (`core/hooks/useChartMargins.ts:234`).
- Horizontal mode renders one DOM node per category with no overlap pass (`overlays/AxisLabels.tsx:331`).
- The shared date-parse cache clears itself at 5,000 entries (`utils/dayjs.ts:36`), and the tick and interval helpers each parse every label (`utils/dates.ts:31`, `:194`).
- After: pick candidates by stride before formatting and measuring, cache widths, and parse dates once per `labels` array.

**P3. Resize recomputes data ranges.**
- Every ResizeObserver frame (`core/hooks/useChartCanvas.ts:103`) gives new dimensions, and `useChartScales` calls `createScales(series, labels, dimensions)` again (`core/hooks/useChartScales.ts:43`, `:70`). That walks all the data, though the value range does not depend on pixels.
- After: compute ranges and stacks once per data change, and only re-range the scales on resize.

**P4. Smaller.**
- `charts/ScatterChart/scatter-data.ts:59` allocates a `NaN` array of length total points for every series. 100 series × 100k points is 10M numbers.
- The tooltip renders a row per series inside a scroller (`overlays/DefaultTooltip.tsx:165`), and the legend a button per item. That starts to cost past a few hundred series.

## Checked and fine

- **Tree-shaking works.** Importing one chart from the built package and minifying gives 37 KB for `Gauge`, 48 KB for `PieChart` and 74 KB for `LineChart`, against 233 KB for everything (dependencies external). `Sparkline` (96 KB) and `BarList` (86 KB) cost more than `LineChart`, because they wrap the full line and bar charts.
- **Imports are safe outside a browser.** No module touches `window` or `document` at import time.
- **Hover.** Hit-testing is O(log n), and listeners and animation frames are removed on unmount.
- **Timezones.** Parsing is independent of the browser zone.
- **Legend.** 30 production files use `config.legend`, and 3 or 4 build one by hand, so the built-in legend is doing its job.

## Open questions

1. #116505, #120197 and #121121 are closed, and no file outside the library builds on `Chart` or `RadialChart`. Does the "custom chart kit stays public" rule still have a user? If the plan is parked, items 19, 30, 32, 61 and 64 can change `ChartProps` and `ChartScales` without a deprecation step.
2. About 45 production files hand-build an empty state beside a chart, and four products wrote a wrapper for it. The first review kept "no empty prop". Is an `empty` slot, rendered in the chart's own box, worth it?

A zero baseline reads as unchanged, as in the compare table. > [!NOTE] > Behavior changes: > - Faster cells are blue, not green. The tooltip's delta stays green. > - "+N more" zooms in place instead of opening a popover. > - The focus event also fires on Escape and the reset button. - Mechanical: the tree building moves unchanged into `traceFlameTree.ts`. ## hog-charts review

Ran the `hog-charts-review` skill against this PR after rebasing it. The parent (#123011) has merged, so the branch now sits on master.

Master's #120236 now also uses `TraceCompareFlame` for the single-trace call tree in the trace view, so the rebase ported that view onto the quill `FlameGraph` too. That needed three optional props in the library, now in [#131637](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/131637) below this PR:

- `FlameNode.color` fills one node (error spans).
- `FlameGraphConfig.groupColors` sets the color per group (the waterfall's service colors), for fills and the legend.
- `FlameGraphProps.onFocusChange` reports zoom changes, which keeps the pinned `tracing trace call tree focused` event.

**Verdict on the first pass:** Request changes. All findings below are fixed in [19a3129](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/129135/commits/19a3129af7bb) here and [112e305](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/131637/commits/112e3050b2e6) in #131637.

**consider:** If two nodes share an explicit `id`, clicking the second one zooms into the first.

The first node wins in `explicitIds`, and focus resolves through ids (`nodeId` → `keyToFocus` → `indexOfId`), so the zoom lands in a different part of the tree and the breadcrumb shows the other call path. Profiles are likely to hit this: the JSDoc calls `id` a "Stable identity", which suggests a function key such as `parse@lexer.ts:12`, and that key repeats under every caller.

Fix: either document in the `FlameNode.id` JSDoc and `chart-types.md` that ids must be unique within the tree, or have `nodeId` use the explicit id only when `explicitIds.get(own) === i` and fall back to the path id otherwise.

issue.title: Always label the latest month on long-range monthly trends charts
issue.body:
## Is your feature request related to a problem?

On a long-range monthly trends insight, the x-axis often has no label for the most recent month. A customer asked for the latest month to be labeled on an all-time insight, so they can tell at a glance where the data ends.

When there are more month labels than fit, the axis keeps labels from left to right and drops any that overlap. The first month is always labeled, and the last one is labeled only if it happens to fit. For example, a monthly axis from February 2023 to November 2026 ends on "October", and November has no label.

To see it, create a trends insight with a monthly interval over about three years or more (for example "All time"), and view it at a normal insight width.

## Describe the solution you'd like

The most recent month is always easy to identify, without losing the first month or the year labels ("2024", "2025") that the axis shows today.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

All of these are in #130547, which won't be merged.

- **Count back from the latest month and keep every nth label.** The latest month always shows, but the first month often loses its label, and year labels get skipped.
- **Short month names ("Oct" instead of "October").** More labels fit on wide charts. With left-to-right thinning, the latest month and the year labels still drop.
- **Calendar steps.** Keep every 1, 2, 3, 6 or 12 months counted from January, so every year label stays, and always add the latest month. The gap before the latest month is uneven, and the start of the data is often unlabeled.

None of these looked right, so the behavior is unchanged.

Not tried yet:

- Mark the latest point some other way, such as a highlighted tick or the latest value at the right edge, instead of relying on the axis labels.
- Rotate labels when they don't fit, instead of dropping them.

## Additional context

- Label thinning: `computeVisibleXLabels` in `packages/quill/packages/charts/src/overlays/AxisLabels.tsx`
- Date tick text: `createXAxisTickCallback` in `packages/quill/packages/charts/src/utils/dates.ts`

**consider:** A bundle can offer a zoom that does nothing.

`canFocus` is always true for a bundle. Zooming into a bundle of N equal tiny siblings sets the window to their combined span. When N is above about width / 3 (roughly 270 siblings at 800 px), each node is still under 3 px, so the row redraws as the same "+N more" cell. Clicking it calls `changeFocus` with the same range, and nothing changes, but the tooltip still says "Click to zoom in".

Fix: set `canFocus` to false when the focus is already this bundle (`focus.kind === 'bundle' && focus.first === cell.index && focus.last === cell.last`), and skip `changeFocus` in `onClick` in that case.

**consider:** The viewport height and the plot width depend on each other, so the chart can flicker.

`rowCount` comes from `computeFlameCells(…, plotWidth, …)`, and nodes under 3 px drop their children, so a narrower plot can have fewer rows. With classic scrollbars (Windows and most Linux setups), going past `maxHeight` adds a scrollbar of about 15 px. The `ResizeObserver` then reports a narrower width, the deepest row can drop out, the content fits, the scrollbar goes away, and the row comes back. It only takes a deepest node near the 3 px cutoff and a row count near `maxHeight / 22`.

Fix: add `[scrollbar-gutter:stable]` here so the width no longer depends on overflow.

**should-fix:** A rounding error in the child layout lets nodes from a neighbouring subtree leak into a zoomed view.

When a parent's children add up to exactly its weight, the last child's `right` is `left + Σ weight·unit`. That sum can land one ulp past the parent's `x1`. The parent's right edge is also the next sibling's `x0`, and that becomes `window.x0` when you zoom into the sibling. So `firstEndingAfter(x1, …, window.x0)` in `computeFlameCells` picks up the overshooting descendants of the left neighbour as cells. They have a large negative `x0` and an `x1` of about 4e-13 px.

We ran this branch's `buildFlameTree` + `computeFlameCells` on a random 4k-node tree:
- 258 of 1,380 zooms included cells that were neither ancestors nor descendants of the focus.
- In trees with uneven depths, the focus gained a blank extra row, because `targetRows` counts the leaked cell's depth.
- In 4 focuses, `HIT_SLOP_PX = 4` made `cellAt(cells, d, 2)` return the leaked node. Hovering the first 4 px showed a tooltip for an unrelated node, and clicking zoomed into it.

Fix: clamp to the parent.
```ts
const right = Math.min(x1[head], left + weightOf(child) * unit)
```
With that change the same probes found no leaked cells, phantom rows or wrong hits. A regression case in `flame-layout.test.ts` would help: zoom into a node whose left sibling's children sum to its full weight, then assert that every cell is in the focus subtree or one of its ancestors.
